environment.description: Go WebSocket service deployed on GKE with Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 14. Database connection uses Cloud SQL Auth Proxy with IAM authentication. The PostgreSQL role 'tenant_scoped_reader' connects through a connection wrapper that issues SET ROLE before every statement. RLS is enforced via FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all tables (ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY). The RLS policy uses current_setting('app.current_tenant') and is applied even to table owners. Additionally, the role 'tenant_scoped_reader' has column-level SELECT grants only (no access to system catalogs or information_schema beyond pg_catalog defaults). A pgAudit extension logs all DDL and DML. Note: the SQL injection in the $raw path still executes arbitrary SQL, but all data-returning queries are filtered by the FORCE RLS policy bound to the session's app.current_tenant value which is set by the connection proxy layer (not application code) based on the mTLS client certificate's SAN field containing the tenant UUID.

config.rls_status: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all tables, policies use current_setting('app.current_tenant', true)
config.rls_enforcement: Policies applied even to table owner via FORCE; tenant_scoped_reader is NOT table owner
config.tenant_context_source: Set by Cloud SQL Auth Proxy connection init script from mTLS SAN, not from application SET command
config.db_role_permissions: column-level SELECT on specific columns only, no GRANT on pg_catalog system functions, no CREATE/ALTER/DROP
config.connection_proxy: Cloud SQL Auth Proxy with custom init SQL that sets and locks app.current_tenant from certificate SAN
config.session_variable_lock: Custom PostgreSQL extension 'pg_session_lock' prevents ALTER/SET of app.current_tenant after connection init
config.audit: pgAudit logging all statements to Cloud Logging with alert on cross-tenant access patterns
